title: Deep Optimizer States: Towards Scalable Training of Transformer Models Using Interleaved Offloading
note: Mechanism is CPU-GPU interleaved offloading of optimizer state driven by intra-iteration GPU memory fluctuation, which is meaningful with one GPU plus large host RAM - exactly this machine's shape (24 GB GPU, 125 GiB RAM). Artifact URL is printed in the paper and the directory contains run scripts and sample logs. Concern: the paper evaluates 7B-70B models across many GPUs, so a scale-down to a ~1B-class model is required; the DataStates DeepSpeed/Megatron-DeepSpeed forks may want a CUDA newer than the system 11.8, which conda can supply within driver 535's compatibility window. Merge note: scout linked the subdirectory https://github.com/DataStates/artifacts/tree/main/deep-optimizer-states .

title: Detecting Transactional Bugs in Database Engines via Graph-Based Oracle Construction
note: TxCheck is a user-space fuzzer plus statement-dependency-graph oracle driving TiDB, MySQL and MariaDB locally; no root, no cluster. Concern: it is a bug-finding tool, so an "improvement" hypothesis has to be about oracle coverage or test-generation throughput rather than system performance, and building three DBMS targets in user space is nontrivial.

title: DEG: Efficient Hybrid Vector Search Using the Dynamic Edge Navigation Graph
note: Graph-based ANN index for hybrid vector queries; single machine

title: COMET: Neural Cost Model Explanation Framework
note: Explanations for learned basic-block cost models (Ithemal vs uiCA) - a learned component inside a compiler toolchain, CPU-only and cheap to run on 16 cores. Open-sourced in the paper. Concern - ground-truth throughputs come from the published BHive dataset measured on other microarchitectures; re-measuring on this Threadripper is not possible with perf_event_paranoid=3, so the study must stay dataset-based.

title: TCO-driven Storage Provisioning for Exascale Data Centers
note: TCO model and optimal workload-to-storage-class solver for exascale storage - the artifact is a self-contained user-space model and solver. Concern: it is a modeling and telemetry study rather than a running storage system

title: Massive-Scale Out-Of-Core UMAP on the GPU
note: Out-of-core GPU UMAP with an explicit single-GPU result (22.7x); batching/spilling strategy is the contribution and is squarely user-space CUDA. Concerns: multi-GPU is optional but is where the headline 74x comes from and the largest datasets exceed the ~257 GB free on /home so scale-down is needed

title: PyTorch 2: Faster Machine Learning Through Dynamic Python Bytecode Transformation and Graph Compilation
note: TorchDynamo/TorchInductor (torch.compile); fully open, runs on a single GPU or CPU. Very large codebase - scope an improvement narrowly (e.g. a guard or fusion heuristic).

title: WAFFLE: Exposing Memory Ordering Bugs Efficiently with Active Delay Injection
note: Active delay injection for concurrency bug detection - user-space instrumentation with no kernel, root or perf dependency. Concern - the implementation targets .NET/C#, so a user-space .NET SDK install is required, and the repo has very little activity beyond the artifact drop.

title: Region-based Content Enhancement for Efficient Video Analytics at the Edge
note: RegenHance is a PyTorch + PyCUDA pipeline (importance prediction, region stitching, super-resolution, detection) that runs on a single GPU; an RTX A5000 is stronger than the edge devices used in the paper, so a scale-down is meaningful and accuracy/throughput are directly measurable. Concerns: the paper evaluates across five heterogeneous edge devices, which cannot be reproduced; the repo README admits it was not reorganized after submission, so build effort is uncertain.

title: OPPerTune: Post-Deployment Configuration Tuning of Services Made Easy
note: RL/bandit-based post-deployment configuration tuning with automatic scoping; released as a Python framework. Concerns: the paper evaluates on Microsoft production services and on microservice benchmarks that normally need Kubernetes, which we cannot run - a local study would have to tune a single-process application or replay offline workloads.

title: AgenticCache: Cache-Driven Asynchronous Planning for Embodied AI Agents
note: Plan-transition cache with an asynchronous background updater for embodied agents - a genuine cache admission/eviction/validation policy question, evaluated in user-space simulators with released code. Concern: needs an LLM backend, either a local 7-8B model or API budget

title: Serf : Streaming Error-Bounded Floating-Point Compression
note: Streaming error-bounded floating-point compression; user-space library

title: CtxPipe: Context-aware Data Preparation Pipeline Construction for Machine Learning
note: Automatic construction of ML data-preparation pipelines; CPU-bound, user space

title: LVMT: An Efficient Authenticated Storage for Blockchain
note: Authenticated key-value storage layer (versioned multipoint trie over an LSM store) evaluated on replayed Ethereum traces on one machine. Rust, user-space, no special hardware. Concern: blockchain framing and a cryptographic (vector-commitment) core, and the AE badge link points at the plotting repo so the benchmark harness above is the substantive artifact.

title: TokenFlow: Responsive LLM Text Streaming Serving under Request Burst via Preemptive Scheduling
note: Preemptive request scheduling plus proactive KV cache swapping between GPU and CPU for text streaming - single GPU plus host memory is a natural scale-down. No official repo found so far

title: Rethinking Key-Value Cache Compression Techniques for Large Language Model Serving
note: Measurement plus released tooling for KV-cache compression in serving - artifact is a reusable benchmark harness, paper used a single A6000 so a single 24 GB A5000 works with 7-8B models - concern: a few configs were sized for 48 GB

title: Hydra: Virtualized Multi-Language Runtime for High-Density Serverless Platforms
note: The Hydra runtime colocates many function sandboxes in one process using GraalVM Native Image Isolates plus Truffle, with per-sandbox checkpoint/restore - all user space, installable in $HOME. Concern - the Hydra *platform* half compares against OpenWhisk and Knative, which need Docker/Kubernetes and root, so the project would have to stay at the runtime/density level.

title: LINE: A Learned Index with Group-Enhanced Leaves and Cache-Optimized Inner Tree
note: learned index with group-enhanced leaves and a cache-optimized inner tree - learned system component - concern: no repo located

title: Felix: Optimizing Tensor Programs with Gradient Descent
note: Gradient-descent search over a differentiable relaxation of TVM/Ansor schedules; evaluated on single GPUs and finishes searches in minutes, which suits a 10-week budget.

title: Sim-Piece: Highly Accurate Piecewise Linear Approximation through Similar Segment Merging
note: Piecewise-linear lossy compression for time series; Java, CPU-only, small datasets - easy to reproduce and extend

title: Galley: Modern Query Optimization for Sparse Tensor Programs
note: Cost-based optimizer/compiler for sparse tensor programs; ML-compiler topic, single node

title: HoneyComb: A Parallel Worst-Case Optimal Join on Multicores
note: Parallel worst-case optimal join engineered for large multicore shared-memory machines

title: RAGPerf: An End-to-End Benchmarking Framework for Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
note: End-to-end RAG serving benchmark that measures throughput host and GPU memory and CPU GPU utilization across vector stores and LLMs; open-sourced and single-node

title: Amalgam: A Framework for Obfuscated Neural Network Training on the Cloud
note: Model/dataset augmentation for obfuscated training; repo URL is printed in the abstract. Vision and NLP models used are modest and fit a single 24 GB A5000; the "cloud" framing is only a deployment story and the measured quantity is per-GPU training overhead, which reproduces locally.

title: Understanding GPU Resource Interference One Level Deeper
note: CUDA microbenchmark suite that isolates interference on block schedulers, compute units, L1/L2 and memory bandwidth, plus a vLLM fork for colocated LLM token generation. Single GPU, fully user space. Concerns - this is an 8-page measurement study rather than a system, so an improvement project would have to extend the methodology or build a policy on top of it; and some GPU counter collection may require admin-enabled profiling, which is unavailable here.

title: Maximus: A Modular Accelerated Query Engine for Data Analytics on Heterogeneous Systems
note: Modular CPU+GPU query engine; concern - the paper also targets DPUs/SmartNICs and disaggregated memory, only the CPU/GPU part is reproducible here

title: Bridging the Indexing Gap in Fused GPU Query Engines
note: Fused GPU bitmap indexing that keeps intermediates in registers. Concern: evaluated on an RTX 5090 D so absolute numbers will differ on Ampere but the technique is single-GPU

title: Refactoring Index Tuning Process with Benefit Estimation
note: learned benefit estimation that skips what-if calls during index tuning

title: CrocSort: Resource-Efficient, Skew-Resilient Parallel External Merge Sort
note: Parallel external merge sort with explicit memory and thread configuration rules and skew-resilient range partitioning; resource-efficiency work on NVMe that fits this host

title: Fair Transaction Processing For Multi-Tenant Databases
note: DRFT fair-share scheduling for transactions - resource-manager policy work evaluated on single-node benchmarks

title: Resource Multiplexing in Tuning and Serving Large Language Models
note: Spatial-temporal multiplexing of LLM fine-tuning and inference on the same GPUs; the smallest configuration is Llama-8B on RTX 3090-class 24 GB GPUs which matches the A5000. Concern: several experiments use 4 GPUs and 70B models that will not fit. Merge note: scout linked the artifact branch https://github.com/llm-db/llmstation/tree/atc25-artifact .

title: AquaPipe: A Quality-Aware Pipeline for Knowledge Retrieval and Large Language Models
note: Pipelines disk-based ANNS retrieval with LLM prefill in a RAG serving system; 7B-class models fit 24 GB

title: DeepContext: A Context-aware, Cross-platform, and Cross-framework Tool for Performance Profiling and Analysis of Deep Learning Workloads
note: Cross-stack profiler correlating Python, framework, C++ and GPU contexts for DL workloads; concerns: GPU hardware counters via CUPTI usually need admin-enabled profiling and CPU perf counters are blocked here, and no official repo was found

title: On Self-Designing Learned Indexes
note: self-designing learned index that searches its own structure with RL and meta-learning - learned system component, in-memory and on-disk

title: CoServe: Efficient Collaboration-of-Experts (CoE) Model Inference with Limited Memory
note: Serving many small expert models under a memory budget with expert placement/switching across memory tiers - fits 125 GiB RAM plus one GPU; concern: no official repo found by GitHub/web search

title: How to Write to SSDs
note: Redesigns LeanStore to write out-of-place cutting flash write amplification by up to 9.8x. Concern: the ZNS and FDP extensions need special SSD interfaces but the core out-of-place design runs on a normal file

title: Automatic Database Configuration Debugging using Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
note: RAG/LLM-based DBMS configuration diagnosis; concern - needs LLM API access

title: Parallel kd-tree with Batch Updates
note: Parallel cache-efficient in-memory kd-tree for a 16-core machine

title: Getting a Handle on Unmanaged Memory
note: ALASKA - compiler plus runtime that adds handles to unmanaged C/C++ so the heap can be compacted; drop-in malloc replacement, user-space only. Main repo is nickwanninger/alaska.

title: Optimistic No-regret Algorithms for Discrete Caching
note: Prediction-assisted (oracle/NN-guided) discrete caching policies with a new optimistic Follow-the-Perturbed-Leader family; evaluated trace-driven on MovieLens and similar request traces. Pure CPU Python, no root, no GPU needed - a natural fit for the machine. Improvement angle - the policies are O(N) per request in the number of files and the paper itself trades performance against complexity; a faster implementation or a real cache integration is a testable hypothesis. Concern - the paper is theory-heavy and the released code is a numerical-experiment harness rather than a cache system so a reproduction may feel thin without extending it to a real workload trace

title: ShadowAQP: Efficient Approximate Group-by and Join Query via Attribute-oriented Sample Size Allocation and Data Generation
note: A learned component inside a query engine - a conditional VAE trained per table that generates samples for approximate group-by/join queries, plus sample-size allocation, outlier-aware sampling and dimension reduction. Core mechanism is single-GPU model training plus sample generation, which fits the A5000 easily. Concern: the paper's baselines run on a 10-node Spark/Hive cluster; on one machine those comparisons must be scaled down to local Spark plus single-node Postgres, which changes absolute speedups but preserves the accuracy-vs-cost hypothesis. Artifact statement in the paper points at the repo. [PVLDB 16(13), added from the vldbgap-2024 shard]

title: Scalable Complex Event Processing on Video Streams
note: Complex event processing over video streams with model invocation scheduling; single GPU

title: Beware of Fragmentation: Scheduling GPU-Sharing Workloads with Fragmentation Gradient Descent
note: scope.md explicitly allows cluster/GPU schedulers "evaluated with simulators or traces": the paper's 6,200-GPU results come from a Go-based Kubernetes scheduler *simulator* replaying public Alibaba traces, which runs as a normal user process on one machine. AE Available+Functional+Reproduced. Concerns: Go must be installed via conda; the real-cluster deployment half of the paper is not reproducible, and simulator-only results weaken an "improvement" claim unless the fragmentation metric itself is the target.

title: Oasis: An Optimal Disjoint Segmented Learned Range Filter
note: learned range filter integrated into RocksDB; a clean single-machine storage project

title: RepCut: Superlinear Parallel RTL Simulation with Replication-Aided Partitioning
note: Parallel RTL simulation by replication-aided partitioning - CPU-only user-space simulator that scales with the 16 cores here  Zenodo AE artifact

title: Beyond Compression: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Lossless Floating-Point Compression
note: Benchmark plus Rust library of lossless floating-point compressors including in-situ query execution on compressed data; single node

title: Janus: Multi-LLM Serving at Production Scale
note: Multi-LLM serving with dual-timescale scheduling, HBM virtualization (xTensor) and device-to-device model fork. Repo exists. Big concern: deployed on 768 devices in production, so the elastic-scaling and bin-packing results have no direct single-GPU analogue - the request scheduler and xTensor memory virtualization do.

title: LogLite: Lightweight Plug-and-Play Streaming Log Compression
note: Streaming lossless log compressor; pure user-space algorithm with released implementation

title: ContextPilot: Fast Long-Context Inference via Context Reuse
note: Context indexing, alignment and de-duplication to raise KV-cache reuse for long-context prefill, with a modular interface to existing engines. Prefill-bound, single-GPU workloads are well within the A5000's reach

title: The Benefit of Hindsight: Tracing Edge-Cases in Distributed Systems
note: Always-on retroactive distributed tracing implemented as a user-space C library plus agent needing no root perf counters or eBPF - Concern: the reference evaluation drives DeathStarBench microservices under Docker across several nodes so it must be re-hosted as multiple processes on one machine - code lives on MPI-SWS GitLab not GitHub

title: Themis: A GPU-accelerated Relational Query Execution Engine
note: Intra- and inter-warp load balancing for GPU query pipelines - GPU work scheduling, runs on a single Ampere GPU in user space

title: FlexLLM: Token-Level Co-Serving of LLM Inference and Finetuning with SLO Guarantees
note: Token-level co-serving of inference and PEFT finetuning on shared GPUs with graph pruning for activation memory - the 80 percent activation-memory saving claim is exactly the kind of thing a 24 GB card can test with LLaMA-3.1-8B. Concern - built on FlexFlow Serve (C++/CUDA) which is a heavy build, and the 32B configurations will not fit.

title: The Hidden Bloat in Machine Learning Systems
note: User-space debloating of ML framework shared libraries including GPU fatbins - no root, no kernel, measures file size, memory and runtime - excellent fit for this machine (repo redirects from negativa-ai/negativa-ml)

title: SpaceExit: Enabling Efficient Adaptive Computing in Space with Early Exits
note: Early-exit adaptive inference plus resource scheduling for satellite imagery; the artifact lists an ordinary CUDA GPU (tested on RTX 4090) and a multi-core CPU. Concern: the paper also uses a Jetson Orin Nano testbed emulating CubeSat hardware that cannot be reproduced

title: ZipServ: Fast and Memory-Efficient LLM Inference with Hardware-Aware Lossless Compression
note: Lossless weight compression plus fused decompress-GEMM kernels; Tensor-Core path exists on Ampere. Concern: FP8/FP4 variants would need Ada or Hopper

title: Scalable Context Orchestration for Serving LLMs Over Voice
note: Context-management middleware for voice LLM serving - explicitly models speaking rate, noise and packet loss in the context it builds. ASR plus 7-8B LLM plus TTS fits on one A5000 and the middleware itself is CPU-side. Concern: no artifact URL in the preprint.

title: SMARTTalk: Teaching SMART Logs to Talk to LLMs
note: Learned component inside a storage system: a representation layer turning SMART telemetry into LLM-consumable form for failure prediction. Public datasets (Alibaba SSD SMART logs, Backblaze) and a 7-8B model fit 24 GB with LoRA

title: A Fast, Efficient, and Strongly-Consistent Object Store
note: Storage-engine paper from the Northeastern group behind LSVD. Included rather than rejected because the abstract could not be retrieved - the ACM DL is unreachable from this host and no preprint or author copy was found, so neither the artifact status nor the exact hardware assumptions could be checked. Concerns - a strongly-consistent object store is likely evaluated on a multi-node cluster and may build on RADOS/Ceph, which would need root; repo is unknown after searching GitHub for LSVD/object-store repos and the authors' pages. Verify before committing to it.

title: Cache-Centric Multi-Resource Allocation for Storage Services
note: HARE is a cache-size-aware multi-resource (cache/IO/CPU) allocation algorithm - a policy problem that is naturally simulated or run in user space, with public Twitter cache traces. Two prototypes also released: https://github.com/WiscADSL/hopperkv and https://github.com/WiscADSL/bunnyfs. Concerns: BunnyFS issues I/O through SPDK, whose setup (hugepages, VFIO binding) normally needs root; HopperKV caches DynamoDB behind Redis and would need DynamoDB-local or an AWS account. The algorithm itself is the tractable target.

title: BLASST: Dynamic BLocked Attention Sparsity via Softmax Thresholding
note: Training-free blocked sparse attention driven by a single softmax threshold, with drop-in kernels for prefill and decode across MHA/GQA/MQA/MLA and a calibration procedure. Concerns: the artifact is delivered as a Docker or Singularity image and neither is installed, so dependencies (TensorRT-LLM, FlashInfer) must be rebuilt with conda; some kernels may assume Hopper features

title: Scaling a Declarative Cluster Manager Architecture with Query Optimization Techniques
note: Declarative cluster manager (Kubernetes scheduler) reduced to constrained optimization; evaluated with trace-driven simulation and an emulated cluster. Concern: real Kubernetes needs root or containers, so only the simulated/emulated path is usable. Merge note: scout linked release tag https://github.com/vmware/declarative-cluster-management/releases/tag/vldb23 .

title: Once Rolling Hashing is Enough: Exploiting Rolling Hash Reuse in Delta Compression
note: Rolling hash reuse across the stages of delta compression for backup storage - CPU-only user-space algorithm, ideal for the 16-core host. No code release found yet

title: OdinANN: Direct Insert for Consistently Stable Performance in Billion-Scale Graph-Based Vector Search
note: On-disk graph ANNS index with direct insert; entirely user space, single node, CPU + NVMe. Code is shipped inside the authors' PipeANN repo (README cites the FAST '26 OdinANN paper and notes PipeANN is integrated into OdinANN). Concerns: paper machine has 512 GB RAM and billion-scale datasets; with 125 GiB RAM and ~257 GB free disk the study must scale down to 10M-100M vectors (SIFT100M-class), which the artifact supports.

title: Eliminating Redundant Feature Tests in Decision Tree and Random Forest Inference on SQL Predicates
note: eliminates redundant feature tests for decision-tree/random-forest inference on SQL predicates, prototyped on DuckDB - an ML inference runtime optimization - concern: no repo located

title: ArrayMorph: Optimizing Hyperslab Queries on the Cloud for Machine Learning Pipelines
note: Cost-based planner choosing chunked reads vs byte-range reads for array data. Concern: targets S3 and Azure - MinIO substitution is needed and the cloud cost model will not transfer

title: SkinnerMT: Parallelizing for Efficiency and Robustness in Adaptive Query Processing on Multicore Platforms
note: Parallel RL-based adaptive query processing on multicore; Java, 16 cores/32 threads is a sensible scale-down of the paper's machine. Merge note: scout linked branch https://github.com/cornelldbgroup/skinnerdb/tree/skinnermt .

title: "Range as a Key" is the Key! Fast and Compact Cloud Block Store Index with RASK
note: User-space in-memory range index for block stores, evaluated trace-driven against ten baseline indexes - ideal single-machine, no-root study. Alibaba EBS traces released at https://tianchi.aliyun.com/dataset/218875. Concern: the SJTU-hosted GitLab (ipads.se.sjtu.edu.cn) did not respond from this network when checked; availability should be re-verified at audit time.

title: TAILCHECK: A Lightweight Heap Overflow Detection Mechanism with Page Protection and Tagged Pointers
note: Implemented as LLVM compiler passes plus an extended mimalloc allocator; relies only on ordinary x86-64 pointer-tag bits and mmap page protection, all reachable without root. LLVM and the SPEC-style benchmarks build in user space. Concerns: the overhead numbers were measured with hardware the report does not fully specify, and the many PROT_NONE guard mappings may bump into the default vm.max_map_count which cannot be raised without root.

title: Understanding Stragglers in Large Model Training Using What-if Analysis
note: The artifact is a trace-driven what-if simulator, not a cluster - it replays a five-month ByteDance trace on a single machine. Available + Functional. Concern: it is a measurement study, so the improvement angle is a better simulator/attribution method rather than a performance win; check that the released trace subset is large enough to support new claims.

title: Virtual-Memory Assisted Buffer Management
note: Buffer pool built on hardware virtual memory - directly a user-space memory-management design and an excellent improvement target. Concern: the second half of the paper (exmap) is a Linux kernel module and cannot be built or loaded without root; only vmcache itself is reproducible here

title: PilotScope: Steering Databases with Machine Learning Drivers
note: platform for plugging ML drivers into PostgreSQL/openGauss; strong base for an improvement project

title: Selectively Uniform Concurrency Testing
note: Randomized concurrency-testing algorithm, pure user-space, cheap to run and easy to extend

title: Effective Performance Issue Diagnosis with Value-Assisted Cost Profiling
note: vProf is a user-space profiler built on Clang/LLVM instrumentation plus a modified gprof SIGPROF sampler - notably it does not need hardware performance counters, which are blocked on this machine. Artifact on Zenodo plus a public GitHub mirror. Concern - reproducing the 15 real-world bugs means building four large applications from source.

title: FlexAttention: A Programming Model for Generating Fused Attention Variants.
note: Compiler-driven programming model for fused attention variants - shipped in PyTorch core with attention-gym as the paper artifact, single GPU - concern: Ampere means no FP8 variants and torch.compile kernel quality differs from H100 numbers

title: CHEHAB RL: Learning to Optimize Fully Homomorphic Encryption Computations
note: Reinforcement learning to drive an FHE compiler optimizer; CPU-only, user-space learned-tuning system

title: Spira: Exploiting Voxel Data Structural Properties for Efficient Sparse Convolution in Point Cloud Networks
note: Single-GPU sparse-convolution engine for point-cloud networks with released code and clear baselines (torchsparse, spconv). Kernel-map construction is a self-contained, improvable CUDA artifact

title: If At First You Don't Succeed, Try, Try, Again...? Insights and LLM-informed Tooling for Detecting Retry Bugs in Software Systems
note: Wasabi is a user-space static-analysis plus fault-injection toolkit for Java/Python systems; runs on one machine, no root. Concern: it needs LLM API access (cost, non-determinism) and its metric is bug-detection precision/recall rather than performance, so a "testable hypothesis" would have to be framed around detection quality or analysis cost. Weakest topic fit of the included set.

title: Mooncake: Trading More Storage for Less Computation — A KVCache-centric Architecture for Serving LLM Chatbot
note: KVCache-centric prefix cache plus a throughput/SLO-aware request scheduler; policy work is pure user space and the repo is large and actively maintained. Concerns - paper evaluates thousands of A800/H800 nodes with RDMA-based prefill/decode disaggregation; on one RTX A5000 the scale-down is a single-GPU vLLM plus Mooncake Store as a local DRAM/SSD KV tier with the TCP transport, and prefill/decode disaggregation must be emulated by time-slicing or simulated. FP8 paths unusable on Ampere.

title: MRV: Enforcing Numeric Invariants in Parallel Updates to Hotspots with Randomized Splitting
note: Randomized splitting of hot numeric records to remove update hotspots while preserving invariants; the mechanism itself is a user-space concurrency technique. Concern: motivation and evaluation lean on large-scale or geo-distributed deployments; no repo confirmed

title: PoWER Never Corrupts: Tool-Agnostic Verification of Crash Consistency and Corruption Detection
note: Verification technique (Verus/Dafny) plus a verified KV store; the proof side is entirely user-space and reproducible on CPU, and the artifact has Available + Functional + Reproduced badges plus a Zenodo DOI. Serious concern: both CapybaraKV and its baselines target Intel Optane persistent memory, which env.md rules out - the performance half of the paper cannot be reproduced without DRAM-backed PM emulation, so a project here would have to be framed around the verification/proof-effort side.
